sections.text: Following the release of Rihanna's seventh studio album, Unapologetic, and its accompanying tour, Rihanna took a step back from music. "I wanted to have a year to just do whatever I want artistically, creatively," the singer said. She then went on to state that this hiatus lasted only a week before she ultimately returned to the  studio. Following the release of three singles in 2015—"FourFiveSeconds" (with Kanye West and Paul McCartney), "Bitch Better Have My Money" and "American Oxygen"—Billboard announced that Rihanna was set to premiere a new single on January 27, 2016, at 8 am EST. The same day, "Work" premiered on several radio stations worldwide, including BBC Radio 1 in the United Kingdom. Subsequently, it was made available for digital download in most countries, worldwide, via the iTunes Store, and was added for streaming on Apple Music, Spotify, and Tidal.

sections.heading: Writing and recording
sections.wikitext:
"Work" was written by [[PartyNextDoor]], [[Drake (musician)|Drake]], [[Rihanna]], [[Monte Moir]], [[Sevn Thomas|Rupert "Sevn" Thomas]], [[Allen Ritter]] and [[Boi-1da|Matthew Samuels]], and was produced by [[Boi-1da]], Sevn Thomas, Ritter, [[Kuk Harrell]] and [[Noah "40" Shebib]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://uk.complex.com/music/2016/01/rihanna-drake-work-song-credits|title=Here's Everyone Listed in the Song Credits for Rihanna and Drake's 'Work'|work=[[Complex (magazine)|Complex]]|last=Ortiz|first=Edwin|date=January 27, 2016|access-date=January 27, 2016|location=United Kingdom|archive-date=March 24, 2016|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160324110747/http://uk.complex.com/music/2016/01/rihanna-drake-work-song-credits|url-status=live}}</ref> In the summer of 2015, Thomas, Ritter, Boi-1da, and Martin Mason, among others, stayed at Drake's house in [[Los Angeles]] for a mid-week period. Thomas described the time spent at the home as a "beat factory, everyone was sitting there working and collaborating with each other."<ref name="complexwriting">{{cite web|url=http://www.complex.com/music/2016/01/producer-sevn-thomas-details-the-process-of-making-rihanna-and-drakes-new-single-work?sr_share=facebook|title=How a Studio Session at Drake's House in Los Angeles Turned Into Rihanna's Next Big Hit|work=[[Complex (magazine)|Complex]]|last=Frydenlund|first=Zach|date=January 27, 2016|access-date=January 27, 2016|archive-date=September 10, 2017|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170910041539/http://www.complex.com/music/2016/01/producer-sevn-thomas-details-the-process-of-making-rihanna-and-drakes-new-single-work?sr_share=facebook|url-status=live}}</ref>

Thomas created a beat which was [[dancehall]]-influenced; he later played it for Boi-1da to which he positively responded, "We're both Jamaican-Canadian. It was just something in our DNA, so it woke him up, and we started remembering all these old dancehall songs from the '90s." Boi-1da came with up idea for sampling an "old school dancehall rhythm" and after that the chords were made with Ritter and past it, "everything went organically". The most recognizable sampling found in the "Work" [[riddim]] is from the 1998 riddim "Sail Away" which was produced by [[Richie Stephens (musician)|Richie Stephens]] and Mikey 2000,<ref name="complexwriting"/> interpolating [[Alexander O'Neal]]'s "[[If You Were Here Tonight]]".<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.jamaicaobserver.com/entertainment/stephens-to-sail-away-with-ascap-award_96121|title=Stephens to sail away with ASCAP Award|work=[[Jamaica Observer]]|date=April 19, 2017|first=Simone|last=Morgan-Lindo|access-date=February 2, 2021|archive-date=February 7, 2021|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210207025903/http://www.jamaicaobserver.com/entertainment/stephens-to-sail-away-with-ascap-award_96121|url-status=live}}</ref>

When the song's music was finished, Boi-1da sent it to PartyNextDoor who wrote the lyrics. "He’s an incredible writer, and he's Jamaican as well. I think so that's how he's able to come up with those vibes and feels," noted Thomas. PartyNextDoor originally wrote the record as a breakup song;<ref>{{Cite web|url = https://www.mtv.com/news/2920107/partynextdoor-rihanna-drake-work-breakup-song/|title = PartyNextDoor Actually Wrote Rihanna and Drake's 'Work' as a Breakup Song|website = [[MTV]]|access-date = March 3, 2022|archive-date = March 3, 2022|archive-url = https://web.archive.org/web/20220303215850/https://www.mtv.com/news/2920107/partynextdoor-rihanna-drake-work-breakup-song/|url-status = dead}}</ref> after Drake heard the song and loved it, he decided to write and record a verse, as well . The original reference track contained Braithwaite's vocals and a tweaked verse from Drake. It leaked as a snippet in February 2016,<ref>{{Cite web|url = https://www.complex.com/music/2016/02/partynextdoor-rihanna-reference-track-work|title = Is This PARTYNEXTDOOR's Reference Track for Rihanna's "Work?" (UPDATE)|website = [[Complex Networks]]|access-date = March 3, 2022|archive-date = March 3, 2022|archive-url = https://web.archive.org/web/20220303215851/https://www.complex.com/music/2016/02/partynextdoor-rihanna-reference-track-work|url-status = live}}</ref> but the full version was released online in April of that year.<ref>{{Cite web|url = https://www.mtv.com/news/2874082/partynextdoor-drake-rihanna-work-reference-track/|title = Here's the Original Version of Rihanna and Drake's 'Work,' Sung by Partynextdoor|website = [[MTV]]|access-date = March 3, 2022|archive-date = March 3, 2022|archive-url = https://web.archive.org/web/20220303215850/https://www.mtv.com/news/2874082/partynextdoor-drake-rihanna-work-reference-track/|url-status = dead}}</ref> Initially, the intention was to keep the song as a collaboration between the two, or to give to [[Alicia Keys]].<ref name="nytimes.com">{{Cite news|url=https://www.nytimes.com/2016/08/17/arts/music/partynextdoor-drake-rihanna-interview.html?_r=4|title=PartyNextDoor is Finding His Voice, and a Bigger Spotlight|newspaper=The New York Times|date=August 16, 2016|last1=Coscarelli|first1=Joe|access-date=March 3, 2022|archive-date=March 3, 2022|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220303215850/https://www.nytimes.com/2016/08/17/arts/music/partynextdoor-drake-rihanna-interview.html?_r=4|url-status=live}}</ref> Shortly thereafter, Braithwaite stayed at Rihanna's home in [[Malibu, California|Malibu]], where he played her the song,<ref name="complexwriting"/> saying afterwards "it was all that she could sing around the house" and it was her "family's favourite song".<ref name="nytimes.com"/>

Rihanna's vocals were recorded by Marcos Tovar and [[Kuk Harrell]] at [[Westlake Recording Studios]], Los Angeles; the latter also served as a vocal producer. Drake's vocals were recorded by Noel Cadastre and [[Noah "40" Shebib]] at the Sandra Gale Studios in California and the SOTA Studios in Toronto. The vocal recording was assisted by Thomas Warren, while additional vocals were provided by PartyNextDoor. Manny Marroquin [[Mixing engineer|mixed]] "Work" at the Larrabee Studios, while Noel "Gadget" Campbell and Shebib did the mixing at the Studio 360 and SOTA Studios in Toronto. The [[Mastering engineer|mastering]] was done by Chris Gehringer at the [[Sterling Sound Studios|Sterling Sound]] in New York City.<ref name="credits"/> "Work" marked the third collaboration between Rihanna and Drake, following "[[What's My Name (Rihanna song)|What's My Name?]]" in 2010 and "[[Take Care (song)|Take Care]]" in 2012.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://pitchfork.com/news/62844-rihanna-and-drake-team-for-work/|title=Rihanna and Drake Team for 'Work'|work=[[Pitchfork Media]]|last=Camp|first=Zoe|date=January 27, 2016|access-date=January 27, 2016|archive-date=January 28, 2016|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160128023906/http://pitchfork.com/news/62844-rihanna-and-drake-team-for-work/|url-status=live}}</ref>

sections.text:
"Work" is a dancehall, reggae-pop and R&B song, with a length of three minutes and thirty-nine seconds. Hugh McIntyre of Forbes described the song as "quite" urban and mixes hip hop influences with "island vibes". Zach Frydenlund of Complex wrote that the song "is slower and very rhythmic with Rihanna showing off her vocal skills over the crafty production." The song is in the C{{Sharp}} Dorian mode (written using the same key signature as G{{Sharp}} minor) in common time with a tempo of 92 beats per minute. The vocals in the song span from F{{Sharp}}<sub>3</sub> to E{{Flat}}<sub>5</sub>. Alexa Camp of Slant Magazine called it "an understated midtempo jam in the vein of Janet Jackson's recent 'No Sleeep', with a percolating beat, sinuous synth lines, and vocal samples stretched and pulled in a way that recalls Jimmy Jam and Terry Lewis's masterful production work on Janet's 1997 album The Velvet Rope." The Guardian{{'s}} Harriet Gibsone wrote: "The glossy, modernist 'Work' skewers elements of dub and dancehall: her voice is at times Auto-Tuned, and a distant sample of what sounds a little like Grace Jones's "My Jamaican Guy" haunts its empty spaces."

Rolling Stone{{'s}} Daniel Kreps wrote the song contains "a tropical house vibe". In contrary, Taj Ran from Billboard wrote the song "isn't part of a new genre that many in the mainstream media are calling 'tropical house.' Anti{{'s}} lead single is undeniably drenched in dancehall, a genre with deep roots in Jamaica's club scene that spun off from reggae in the 1970s." According to The Atlantic{{'}}s Spencer Kornhaber, the single has "strangely unfinished quality" that features its verses, choruses and bridge fade into themselves, "forgoing soft-to-loud explosions or exciting rhythmic changes". He also noted that, Boi-1da also tries to create "escalation" in the song by adding additional drums for the second chorus, flutes, autotuned harmonies and back-off piano. The New York Times{{'}} Jon Caramanica noted Rihanna at times "barely even relies on words, truncating her syllables past patois to something far less exact." Lyrically, "Work" is "about working for a paycheck no matter what else is going on in your life." Additionally, it focuses on "a fragile relationship" that can be seen in the lines, "If I get another chance to, I would never, oh never, neglect you," which Rihanna sings.
